title: Seagulls Are Eating Whales Alive, and 99% of Calves Carry the Scars

scenes.text: Something is eating whales alive off Argentina. It weighs two pounds.
scenes.keywords: kelp gull landing on whale back

scenes.text: Kelp gulls land on a resting right whale and peck through the skin to the blubber underneath.
In the 1970s, about 2 percent of mothers and calves carried gull wounds. By the 2000s, it was 99 percent.
scenes.keywords: southern right whale mother and calf aerial

scenes.text: The gulls learned to go for the calves. By the 2000s the babies had more wounds than their mothers, spread over more of their backs.
Attacked pairs nurse less, rest less and play less. More than 600 calves died at the nursery between 2003 and 2014.
scenes.keywords: whale calf swimming with mother underwater

scenes.text: Scientists photographed 2,680 mother and calf pairs to prove it. Two pounds of seagull, against forty tons of whale. The gull is winning.

description:
Kelp gulls at Península Valdés, Argentina, peck skin and blubber from the backs of living southern right whales.
Aerial photos from 1974 to 2011 show the share of mothers and calves with gull wounds rising from about 2 percent in the 1970s to 99 percent in the 2000s; calves now carry more lesions than their mothers, attacked pairs nurse and rest less, and more than 600 calves died at the calving ground between 2003 and 2014 (Marón et al., PLOS ONE, 2015).
Which animal would you never have guessed could hurt a whale?
subject: kelp gull on whale
first_comment: Older calves carry more wounds than younger ones, and the damage grows through every calving season. Which other tiny animal bullies a giant?
